A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DRPruning. Their complete main texts and appendices are readable, and retained methods, experiments, equations, and displays can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original pruning, continued-pretraining, instruction-tuning, multilingual, and domain-level experiments, plus mask-similarity and model-size analyses in Appendix B.

after.justification: V2 retains those original results and adds prompt-robustness, efficiency, domain-granularity, and translation instruction-tuning experiments in Appendices B.3-B.6.

M1.justification: The core pruning procedure, DRO objective, scaling-law reference losses, and reference-ratio updates remain unchanged. Appendix B.4 introduces parallel data-ratio computation with a one- to two-step update delay, a limited procedural adaptation.

E1.justification: V2 retains the original coverage and adds machine-translation instruction tuning using News-Commentary training data and FLORES-200 validation/test sets across 14 directions, including German, Indonesian, and Hindi (B.6). This substantially extends task coverage. The finer CC/C4 partitions in B.5 reuse existing data.

E2.justification: Corresponding retained experiments preserve their comparator sets, including Sheared Llama/ReSheared, Pythia, Constant, naive DRO, and the multilingual reference models. New experiments reuse ReSheared or compare DRPruning variants; they introduce no new baseline algorithm.

E3.justification: V2 adds five-prompt evaluation, a 0.5B target with 24k continued-pretraining steps, 1600-step coarse/fine domain comparisons, and 2k-step translation instruction tuning evaluated with BLEU. These introduce substantial new protocols; the original training budgets and evaluation settings are retained.

E4.justification: Appendices B.3-B.6 add prompt-sensitivity tests, parallel-update efficiency checks and extreme-compression analysis, coarse-versus-fine domain segmentation experiments, and translation data-allocation analysis. The original mask-similarity and larger-source-model analyses remain. Section 5.4 mainly relocates existing hyperparameter analysis.

E5.justification: Beyond the retained mask-similarity SEM reporting, v2 adds paired t-tests for downstream performance across five prompt variants. Appendix B.3 reports p-values of 0.0458 for 1.3B, 0.0312 for 2.7B, and 0.0032 combined. These concern prompt variation; additional independent training runs are not established.

E6.justification: Matched original result tables retain their numerical entries. New tables add prompt-level scores, runtime measurements, domain cross-entropies, and translation outcomes. For example, Table 19 reports average BLEU of 20.4 for DRPruning versus 18.0 for ReSheared, alongside an EN-HI disadvantage of 1.5 versus 5.6.

T1.justification: Equations 1-6 retain the same pruning constraints, DRO formulation, scaling-law model, distribution constraint, and reference-ratio update. V2 introduces no new theorem, proof, or substantive mathematical derivation.

C1.justification: The introduction refocuses its headline superiority claim from Sheared Llama and other LLMs to data-scheduling methods. The principal claims about balanced pruning, distribution robustness, and broader applicability remain, so this is a limited change in claimed comparison scope.

C2.justification: V2 adds a specific failure boundary at 0.5B, interprets finer partitioning as increasing the difficulty of fixed hyperparameter selection, and explains translation distribution collapse through excessive sampling of small domains. It also clarifies the unfavorable comparison with public 2.7B Sheared Llama and updates the remaining applicability limitations.

D1.justification: V2 supplies the five evaluation prompts per task, CPU overhead and parallel-update details, four-A800 hardware information, the 0.5B architecture, MiniLM/k-means domain partitioning, validation/test sample counts, and translation sampling and training settings. These substantially expand reproducibility information beyond the retained Appendix A.

R1.justification: V2 adds references supporting the new work, including ParroT, FLORES, WMT23, MiniLM, and DeepSeek-R1, plus several introductory citations. It removes references including Bang et al., Duchi et al., and Levy et al. The central positioning around structured pruning, Sheared Llama, and DRO remains.

P1.justification: V2 extensively edits the abstract, introduction, and methodological and experimental exposition. It moves the workflow summary to the start of Section 3, reorganizes existing hyperparameter analysis into Section 5.4, and moves the multilingual data description into Appendix A.2. These changes substantially reshape presentation beyond the added experiments.

P2.justification: V2 adds multi-prompt comparison tables, a full prompt-template table, and efficiency, domain, and translation tables (13-20). It also redraws the sentence-generation workflow, resizes and relocates retained displays, changes highlighting and captions, and moves the former Figure 5 to Figure 6 without adding a new analysis there.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens validation through direct tests of prompt sensitivity, scheduling overhead, domain granularity, and scheduler use during translation instruction tuning (B.3-B.6). It also documents extreme-compression failure and supplies detailed reproduction settings. These address important evidential gaps in v1's robustness, efficiency, and broader-applicability arguments. The original scores remain unchanged, and prompt-based significance tests still do not establish robustness across independent training runs.
